title: How to Find Product-Market Fit, Measure Retention, and Accelerate Growth

segments.speaker: Lenny Rachitsky
segments.text: Gustaf, you have seen thousands of companies go through Y Combinator and previously led growth at Airbnb. What does a real product-market fit retention curve look like?

segments.speaker: Gustaf Alströmer
segments.text: The classic test of product-market fit is whether your cohort retention curve flattens out parallel to the x-axis. If your curve continuously slopes downward toward zero over months, you do not have PMF, regardless of how fast top-of-funnel signups are growing. You cannot pour marketing budget on a product that churns everyone out.

segments.speaker: Gustaf Alströmer
segments.text: At Airbnb, we discovered that the single biggest lever for growth was host activation in the first 14 days. If a new host received their first booking inquiry within two weeks, their likelihood of remaining an active host for the next 12 months increased by more than 300%. Growth teams should obsess over the initial time-to-value milestone.

segments.speaker: Gustaf Alströmer
segments.text: When founders ask what good retention is at YC, we say: for consumer subscription apps, 30% retention at month 12 is top tier. For B2B software, 80% logo retention at year one is baseline, and top quartile is 90% plus with expanding net revenue retention.
